title: Clark vs UM: tuition, size, location
summary: Clark University (Clark) versus University of Miami (UM). Also searched as UM vs Clark. Scorecard table is sourced; prose is checked against those facts. UniRepository is not affiliated with either school.

sections.heading: How they differ
paragraphs: Clark University and the University of Miami (Clark vs UM) are both private nonprofit institutions, as indicated by their ownership codes reported by College Scorecard. Clark University, located in Worcester, has an undergraduate enrollment of 2,214 students, whereas the University of Miami in Coral Gables enrolls 12,913 undergraduates. Tuition costs for in-state students are slightly lower at Clark University, with a rate of $58,867 compared to the University of Miami's $62,616. These differences highlight variations in size, location, and tuition between Clark University vs University of Miami (Clark vs UM).

sections.heading: Cost
paragraphs: Cost is a significant factor when comparing Clark University and the University of Miami (Clark vs UM). Both institutions charge the same tuition for in-state and out-of-state students, with Clark University setting tuition at $58,867 and the University of Miami at $62,616. Despite the similarity in tuition fees, the median debt for students who complete their degrees differs notably. Clark University graduates have a median debt of $26,759, which is higher than the University of Miami's median debt of $17,500. These figures provide insight into the financial commitments students may face at each university, reflecting differences in student borrowing and potentially financial aid availability. Overall, the cost comparison between Clark vs UM reveals that while tuition is comparable, the debt burden upon graduation varies.

sections.heading: Learning model and campus
paragraphs: Clark University and the University of Miami (Clark vs UM) offer distinct learning environments shaped by their campus locations and student populations. Clark University is situated in Worcester, Massachusetts, and serves an undergraduate body of 2,214 students, fostering a smaller campus community. In contrast, the University of Miami, located in Coral Gables, Florida, enrolls a significantly larger undergraduate population of 12,913 students, reflecting a more extensive campus setting. These differences in enrollment size and geographic location contribute to varied campus experiences and learning models at Clark University vs University of Miami (Clark vs UM).

paragraphs: Clark University and the University of Miami (Clark vs UM) are both accredited institutions, ensuring that they meet established standards of quality in higher education. sections.heading: Pick Clark if
paragraphs: Pick Clark if you prefer a private nonprofit university with a moderately selective admission rate of about 39.5%. Clark University offers a tuition rate of $58,867 for in-state students, which is competitive among private institutions. Additionally, Clark boasts a completion rate of approximately 76.9% within 150% of the expected time, indicating a strong likelihood of degree attainment. These factors make Clark University a suitable choice for students seeking a private institution with reasonable selectivity, manageable tuition, and a solid track record of student success.

sections.heading: Pick UM if
paragraphs: Pick the University of Miami if you are seeking a private nonprofit institution with a highly selective admission rate of 18.9%. The University of Miami charges $62,616 for in-state tuition, which is slightly higher than some comparable private universities. It also has a strong completion rate, with 83.68% of students finishing their degrees within 150% of the expected time. These factors suggest that the University of Miami may be a good fit for students prioritizing selectivity and a high likelihood of timely degree completion.
